name: Gateway of India
desc: A stone arch by the harbour that watched an empire leave. Sea spray, pigeons, boat horns — the classic Mumbai hello, free forever.

name: Marine Drive
desc: The Queen's Necklace: a curve of streetlights along the sea. Sit on the wall at midnight, count waves, fix your whole life. Free.

name: Elephanta Caves
desc: Ferry out to an island where giant Shiva sculptures were carved into rock 1,400 years ago. Absolute someday-list core.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus
desc: A railway station dressed like a gothic palace — gargoyles, domes, two million commuters. The commute IS the museum.

name: Juhu Beach
desc: Sunset beach where the whole city shows up for sea air and snack-stall smoke. A free show every single evening.

name: Haji Ali Dargah
desc: A white shrine floating at the end of a causeway that vanishes at high tide. Timing is everything; entry is nothing.

name: Crawford Market
desc: A Victorian market hall buzzing with mangoes, spices and chaos in the best possible ratio. Window-shopping smells amazing here.

name: Sanjay Gandhi National Park
desc: An actual leopard-holding national park inside city limits, plus 2,000-year-old cave monasteries. Under a buck to enter.

name: Hanging Gardens
desc: Terraced gardens on Malabar Hill with hedge animals and sunsets over the whole bay. Old-school, free, quietly elite.

name: Chor Bazaar
desc: The legendary 'thieves market' — gramophones, brass, old film posters. Treasure hunting is free; leaving empty-handed is hard.
